K_problems.problem: 25 required fields, can't save part-way, session ends after 10 minutes
K_problems.why: P1/P5 have 15-minute bursts on a phone and will lose everything. The P2/P3 owners don't hold half these answers. Engagements die before I ever see them.

K_problems.problem: Required fields force answers clients don't have (KPI 2, Constraint 3, Risk appetite 1-10, Mission/Vision, Preferred methodology)
K_problems.why: This is my nightmare at the input end. People type filler to get past the * fields, and the AI then treats that filler as fact. I can't tell a real constraint from a made-up one, so invented inputs turn into invented conclusions.

K_problems.problem: Jargon: EngagementSpec, EvidenceItems, M02 critical gaps, gap_01 sales_tx, provenance class: observed, ISIC, Error 422, #A7F3
K_problems.why: Clients don't know what's being asked, so they upload the wrong file or nothing. This is internal schema leaking into the screen, and it makes my firm look like a database instead of a consultancy.

K_problems.problem: Red/green dots are the only status signal, and nothing says what they mean
K_problems.why: P6 (NVDA user) can't see them at all, and colour-blind users can't either. Even sighted users don't know if red means missing, invalid or urgent.

K_problems.problem: Upload is drag-and-drop only, with no button
K_problems.why: It doesn't work for keyboard or screen-reader users (P6) or on phones (P1, P5), so a whole segment can't give me data.

K_problems.problem: 'Error 422: schema mismatch' toast that vanishes after 3 seconds
K_problems.why: It doesn't say what's wrong, shows no example of a good file, and disappears before a screen reader or a slow reader catches it. The client retries blindly or gives up, and I'm not told.

K_problems.problem: No 'I don't have this', 'someone else has it' or 'invite the data owner' option, and no 'why we need it' or 'how to get it'
K_problems.why: Hospital and government data needs a second approver and 2-6 weeks, and the manufacturer CFO delegates to an analyst. With one user and an upload box, clients get stuck with no route out. Missing data can't be declared honestly, so it gets faked or the engagement silently stalls.

K_problems.problem: 10-minute session timeout during a data step that takes days or weeks
K_problems.why: People get logged out mid-export and lose their place. This is guaranteed friction for the people who do the data pulls.

K_problems.problem: The status screen is a spinner and 'processing' with no step, ETA, next action or contact
K_problems.why: Clients can't tell whether they're waiting on us or we're waiting on them, so they sit stuck for days. That's my other nightmare: nothing surfaces it to me either.

K_problems.problem: Upload doesn't capture data dates, coverage or who exported it
K_problems.why: I can't spot stale inputs. A 6-week-old export looks the same as yesterday's, and 'provenance: observed' is only a label with no as-of date.

K_problems.problem: No approval gates are visible: framing, data request and report approval are missing from the flow
K_problems.why: It breaks my rule that nothing reaches the client unapproved. The client may think 'processing' means it's already being worked on, before I've approved the framing.

K_problems.problem: No Arabic, no formal deliverable, no tablet or phone layout
K_problems.why: Government (P3) can't use it at all, and phone-first owners struggle.

K_problems.problem: Asks for budget, currency and trade licence before any value is shown
K_problems.why: A pre-revenue founder (P5) may have no licence, and owners balk at disclosing budget up front. That's a drop-off before we even understand the problem.

K_problems.problem: No upload confirmation of what was received (rows, date range, columns understood)
K_problems.why: The client can't verify, and I can't see whether the file actually covers the period a claim relies on.

walkthrough: 0-3 min: open the inbox and sort 7 threads. There's no stage or urgency at a glance, so I open them one by one to find the held messages.

3-15 min: 2 framings. I scroll each chat to rebuild context, then read the summary card. I check that the 'other possible causes' weren't invented beyond what the client said (about 6 min each). Approve one; edit one.

15-37 min: report 1, a long chat message with expandable sections. I scroll back through the thread to find which upload fed which number. A file from 6 weeks ago is buried 40 messages up, and nothing tells me its date. I spot-check the 3 biggest numbers. I approve without catching it, because the stale figure wasn't one I traced.
37-57 min: report 2. Nothing shows a checker verdict next to the claim. I read it fully and the claim feels a bit strong, so I soften the wording myself. I'm not confident I fixed the right thing.
57-65 min: open the 2 analysis threads just to confirm nothing is held. 'I'm analysing' tells me nothing about progress.

65-75 min: the stuck client's thread has no held message, so it never shows in my approval inbox. I'd only notice if I scrolled all 7 threads looking at last-message dates. Realistically I skip it this Monday.
A.quote: It's lovely for the client and terrifying for me. I'm approving chat bubbles with no idea where the numbers came from, and the client who's gone quiet is invisible because silence doesn't need approving.
A.client_side_comment: It's the friendliest start and good for P1/P5 on a phone. But a long thread loses the data checklist, and clients scroll to find what's still owed. The report-as-chat-message feels unofficial for the hospital board or government (who need a formal PDF in Arabic). There's also a risk that the AI's follow-up questions turn into consultancy promises I haven't approved.

walkthrough: 0-4 min: scan the admin table of 7 rows (stage, % data, last activity, flags). This is the best overview of the three.

4-8 min: the stuck client shows 'Data 40%, last activity 4 days ago'. I catch it, but the table doesn't say why (no access? wrong file? waiting on IT?), so I open the engagement and message the client.
8-22 min: 2 framings. I read the wizard output. KPIs picked from suggestions look plausible but may not be what the client really means. About 7 min each.

22-46 min: report 1 in the full editor. It's formal and long (exec summary, methodology, appendix). There are no per-finding source dates. The 'flags' column might mention data age, but nothing ties it to a specific number. I trace numbers manually through the appendix, run out of patience and miss the 6-week-old figure.

46-66 min: report 2. If the flags include the checker's dispute, I search the report for it. The comments sidebar helps me note it, but approval is for the whole report, so I can't fix one finding and release the rest. I send the whole thing back.
66-70 min: glance at the 2 analysis rows, where the % progress tiles look fine.
C.quote: The table tells me where to look but not what's wrong. Percentages don't catch an old file, and 'approve whole report' means I either rubber-stamp or redo everything.
C.client_side_comment: Government and the CFO will like the formal PDF/Word. But the 5-step wizard is a heavier version of K's form, and clients will still invent KPIs and constraints to get through it. A dashboard of percentages doesn't tell P1/P5 what to do next, and nothing handles the case where 'someone else has the data'.

walkthrough: 0-2 min: open the 'Needs you' queue, already sorted: 'Client stuck 4 days on data', 'Checker disagrees with AI' on report 2, 'Report ready, warning: old data' on report 1, then 2 framings.
2-7 min: stuck client. The data item shows they clicked 'Someone else has this' but the invite was never accepted. I nudge the data owner and send the client a short note. Done.

7-19 min: report 2, finding by finding. Next to the disputed finding I see the checker's verdict and the evidence. I downgrade it to 'Weak' with a reason and send it back to the AI with a note to retest. I approve the other findings.

19-29 min: report 1. The old-data warning sits next to the finding that uses the 6-week-old file. I decide to either ask the client for a fresh export or state the as-of date explicitly. I edit the finding, approve the rest and release it with the caveat.
29-37 min: 2 framings, about 4 min each. 'What we understood' with suspected and alternative causes is quick to verify. Approve both.
37-39 min: the analysis engagements aren't in the queue, which is correct. I glance at their trackers to confirm the expected dates.
B.quote: This is the one where I'm reviewing exceptions instead of hunting for them. The warning sits next to the number, which is exactly where I need it.
B.client_side_comment: Best for my clients. The 'Your next step' card fixes 'am I waiting or are they?', the data checklist with why/how/invite/'we don't have it' matches the hospital, government and CFO realities, and 'How sure are we?' per finding protects me from overclaiming. Concerns: the page gets long for P1/P5 on a phone, so collapse finished sections. 'Results expected Thu' dates must be ones I can actually hit, or they become broken promises. Clients may also use 'Ask a question' to reopen findings I've already approved.

interrogation.a: Having no link from each number in a report to its source file, that file's as-of date and the checker's verdict. If I have to trace numbers by hand, I either blow my 1-hour budget or approve blind, and approving blind is how an invented or stale number reaches a client.
interrogation.b: An exceptions-first queue (stuck clients with days-stuck timers, checker disputes, stale or unsupported-number warnings) and per-finding evidence that shows the source, date range and checker verdict. I also need approval per finding so I can approve clean findings in bulk, a hard block on release while any warning is unresolved, and a 'what changed since I last saw it' diff on resubmitted drafts.
interrogation.c: In B: (1) Put an as-of date and source on every number, with a staleness rule per engagement (e.g. older than 30 days triggers a warning), and block release until each warning is resolved or explicitly accepted with a note. (2) Show a time-spent counter per engagement against my 1-hour budget. (3) Separate 'stuck' from 'expected wait', so a hospital waiting on its 2-6 week data-protection sign-off doesn't trip the stuck alarm every day, while a genuinely silent client does after 48 hours. (4) Add a one-line portfolio strip for engagements not needing me, showing expected date versus slipping. (5) Make framing approval quick on a phone. (6) Add a 'preview as client' view before release, including the Arabic version.
interrogation.d: Make 'number lineage' a rule: the AI can't put any figure in a draft without a clickable trace to the source cell or connector pull, and any number without a trace is auto-flagged as 'unsupported' before I see it. Also send a daily 2-minute digest email ('3 things need you; 1 client silent for 4 days; nothing else'), and keep a signed approval audit trail per release so I can show a client exactly what I checked.
